description:
Create, list, print, copy, delete and render notes. Each note is named by its stem.

Subcommands:
  new --type TYPE --topic TOPIC --thread THREAD [--person P] [--counterparty C] [--location L] — create a note and print its path
  list [FILTER] [--json] — every note, oldest first: stem, date, type, threads, topic
  cat STEM — print a note
  last — print the path of the newest note
  copy STEM — copy a note to a new timestamp; ' COPY' is added to its topic
  delete STEM -y — permanently delete a note
  pdf STEM [--out DIR] — render to markdown and PDF (callouts, action table); print both paths
  minutes STEM [--out DIR] — render meeting minutes: agreements, resolutions, action items
  agenda STEM [--out DIR] — render a meeting agenda: the note with its outcome sections emptied

Args:
  STEM    filename without .md, e.g. 2026-09-10-14-30-00; get it from `notes list`
  FILTER  case-insensitive text matched in any column

Flags:
  new:
    --type T            required; Meeting|Correspondence|Workshop|Report|Log|Research|Recipe
    --topic TEXT        required; must not be empty
    --thread THREAD     required; 'Kind/Name', name or wikilink; repeatable; the note is filed under the first
    --person NAME       Meeting and Correspondence only; repeatable; linked when people/<Name>.md exists
    --counterparty TEXT Meeting only
    --location TEXT     Meeting only
  list:
    --json              JSON output
  delete:
    -y, --yes           required to confirm
  pdf, minutes, agenda:
    --out DIR           output directory (default: the user's Downloads folder); writes <stem>.md and <stem>.md.pdf

Examples:
  ["new", "--type", "Meeting", "--topic", "Scope review", "--thread", "Projects/Northwind", "--person", "Sam Rivera", "--counterparty", "Northwind"]
  ["list", "northwind"]
  ["cat", "2026-09-10-14-30-00"]
  ["minutes", "2026-09-10-14-30-00", "--out", "out"]

Notes:
  Notes live at threads/<Kind>/<Name>/notes/<YYYY-MM-DD-HH-MM-SS>.md. `new` creates the file and prints its path; write the body by editing that file.
  `new` adds a REF: line to buffer.md. It reaches the thread's log on the next `buffer flush`.
  Every subcommand except `new` first ingests ACTION: lines into TASK anchors, which rewrites notes and logs in place.
  `delete` is permanent.
  pdf, minutes and agenda need pandoc and xelatex.
  Exit 1 means one of: a malformed stem, an empty --topic, a flag used with the wrong --type, no notes in the vault, or a failed PDF render.
